newsitem.title: UK: ICI sees Tioxide float in next 18 months.
newsitem.headline: ICI sees Tioxide float in next 18 months.

text.p: Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc said on Thursday that it expected to float its titanium dioxide operations in the next 18 months.

In a telephone interview with Reuters group finance director Alan Spall said "we are looking at something over the next 18 months... having come to the decision that Tioxide is better as an independent organisation."
Spall said the net asset value of the business is $700 million and ICI was talking to advisers about the likely flotation price.
He said ICI had taken the view that Tioxide, which is a major component of paint, would be better separated from its fast-expanding paint operations.
Tioxide prices stumbled badly in 1996, but Spall told Reuters he expected them "to move upward sharply this year".
He noted that sales volumes grew in the second half of 1996, while weaker prices had "dissuaded people from putting in new capacity".
"The supply and demand balance looks good over the next 18 months," Spall added.
